name: noahisarider
summary: Recent reading notes: looped models and diffusion LMs, post-training and RL, plus some human-AI collaboration.

papers.title: Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models
papers.authors: Zhihan Yang, Wei Guo, Jean-Marie Lemercier, et al.
papers.note: Sigma, a large-scale continuous diffusion LM. The speed-up story is not mysterious: DDIM cuts the number of denoising rounds, and PDD merges several rounds of prediction into a single model call.

papers.title: Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part II: Rethinking at Fixed Points
papers.authors: Benhao Huang, Chufan Shi, Junlin Chen, et al.
papers.note: If a looped LM's state nearly stops changing, the path to that point stops mattering — truncated backprop, a 3x smaller KV cache and a student that prefills ~1.8x faster all fall out of it. A learned depth prior plus orthogonal injection is what makes the fixed point reliable.

papers.title: Finetuning with Sampling: SFT Learns Better Than You Think
papers.authors: Aayush Karan, Sitan Chen, Yilun Du
papers.note: Treats SFT's generalization problem as a data problem rather than an objective problem: projection sampling reshapes expert traces toward the base model's distribution, and plain SFT then rivals RL post-training. Worth noting the theory assumes exact MH while the implementation is an approximate acceptance rule.

papers.title: Looped Diffusion Transformer
papers.authors: Yong Xien Chng, Tianyi Chen, Wenwen Tong, et al.
papers.note: A 260M DiT that loops its middle blocks beats a model 6.5x larger: deep supervision on every loop, plus an orthogonal-projection attention (XSA) that stops repeated loops from washing out spatial information.

papers.title: Sharpening Tax in Post-Training
papers.authors: Changdae Oh, Qi Zeng, Qi Qi, et al.
papers.note: RL post-training pushes tasks toward 'always solved or never solved', costing pass@k coverage. The Sharpening Tax quantifies the loss; PTGS raises the sampling temperature on hard prompts and pays a smaller tax. Also a good model of how to turn a broad controversy into a verifiable research chain.

papers.title: Information-Time Proximal Policy Optimization
papers.authors: Yongcheng Zeng, Xinyu Cui, Yan Song, et al.
papers.note: Token distance is not information distance. InfoPPO re-derives discounting and clipping in 'information time' using per-state uncertainty, keeping terminal rewards alive in long reasoning chains instead of over-attenuating them.

papers.title: Generative AI and Human Knowledge Sharing: Evidence from a Natural Experiment
papers.authors: Y. Su, K. Zhang, Q. Wang, L. Qiu
papers.note: A Quora policy shock analysed with DID: embedding AI answers raised human answer volume by ~5.5% and length by 22.5% — no crowding out. The mechanism they isolate is an AI-conformity effect: people align their answers to AI as a trusted source, confirmed by a follow-up experiment.

papers.title: Collaborative human-AI trust (CHAI-T): A process framework for active management of trust in human-AI collaboration
papers.authors: Melanie J. McGrath, Andreas Duenser, Justine Lacey, Cécile Paris
papers.venue: Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humans
papers.note: Treats trust as something you actively manage across a teaming lifecycle rather than calibrate once: three classes of antecedents plus team processes and performance phases, aiming at the zone between rejection and over-reliance.

papers.title: AI Systems and AI Agents as Cognitive Participants: Empirical Evidence of Problem Formation in Decision Systems
papers.note: Three empirical illustrations — semiconductor manufacturing, engineering design, logistics — of AI moving upstream: no longer only solving given problems, but shaping what counts as an anomaly, a feasible design, or a requirement.
